versions.text: Criterion: Verify that the propeller system can safely and reliably operate in world wide environments as required by the system specification. Standard: All environmental conditions (e.g., ice accretion and separation, distortion, sand and dust ingestion, water ingestion) do not adversely affect propeller performance and operability beyond the air vehicle specification requirements. The design usage includes missions and mission mix, usage parameters, externally applied forces, operating envelope, engine attitude limits, ambient temperature distribution, icing environment conditions, corrosive atmosphere conditions, acoustic environment, and engine performance retention characteristics. The loads and environment spectra represent the service life within the design utilization distribution such that the average usage of the system will meet the service life. Method of Compliance: Propeller system components are verified for expected usage and environmental conditions using analyses, component test, and ground/flight tests.

Standard: Design usage, duty cycles addressing all sources of repeated loads, and environmental exposure applicable to the type design being certified are defined and validated. All source material (e.g., military specifications, contract requirements, program documents) is identified, and any modification of source material for the type design being certified is substantiated. Design usage definitions and environments include the following: a. Mission definition and percent utilization. b. Usage statistics. c. Time at flight envelope extremities (e.g., 10 hours at any point in envelope). d. Reverse pitch and feathering usage. e. Propulsion system operating envelope. f. Attitude limits and exposure times. g. Ambient temperature distributions and percent utilization. h. Reduction gearbox extractions and extraction duty cycle (e.g., loaded accessory pads). i. Externally-applied forces (g’s, rotational rates and accelerations). j. Installed temperature, pressure, and vibration environment. k. Acoustic noise environment (installed and uninstalled). l. Icing environment. m. Sand and dust environment. n. Corrosion environment. o. Non-operating and transportation environment. p. Windmilling envelope. q. Cross-wind envelope. r. Electromagnetic environment. The damage content of simplified or composite duty cycles defined for analysis and test are shown to be equivalent to, or more severe than, that of the full mission usage set. Method of Compliance: Prior to entering flight test, verify the standard by the following method(s): Examination.
(1) Examine design documentation or other source material to verify that all design usage, duty cycles, and environments necessary for the type design being certified are defined and valid. Sources are cited and modification of any source material is substantiated. Analysis.
  (1) Analysis defines usage and duty cycles for design, analysis, and test. Damage equivalency of resultant duty cycles is substantiated.
